bug_description: Bank account balance becomes inconsistent during concurrent withdrawals. Multiple goroutines spawned to withdraw funds result in incorrect final balance. Money mysteriously disappears from the account.

hypotheses.hypothesis_text: The lack of mutex protection will cause lost updates when multiple goroutines concurrently read, modify, and write the balance field.
The absence of mutex protection will cause money to be lost during concurrent withdrawal operations.

steps: Run the buggy version 10 times, recording final balance each run
Calculate average final balance and percent error
experiments.actual_observations: Buggy version (no mutex): Final balance $9950 out of expected $5000 - consistently lost $4950 per run (49.5% error). This proves read-modify-write is not atomic. Fixed version (with mutex): Final balance exactly $5000 across all runs - 0% error rate. Mutex protection makes operations atomic, preventing race conditions. Hypothesis is SUPPORTED: absence of mutex causes money loss.

fix_description: Added sync.Mutex field to BankAccount struct. Protected Withdraw() read-modify-write operation with Lock()/Unlock() calls. This ensures only one goroutine can execute the critical section at a time, making the operation atomic and preventing lost updates.

metadata.prediction: Without mutex protection, when 100 goroutines each attempt to withdraw $50 from a $10,000 account, the final balance will be greater than $5,000 (the mathematically correct value), indicating lost updates due to race conditions.
